name: Weird Green
lede: Weird Green is a bright, slightly minty green from the 2010 xkcd color survey, named with a plain subjective reaction rather than any object or place.

sections.title: A reaction, not a reference
sections.body:
Unlike a modifier such as *dark* or *light*, the word *weird* does not describe a hue or a lightness; it records a volunteer's impression of the swatch during the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. Who first typed it, and why this shade struck them as weird rather than merely bright, is not recorded [1]. Its origin is undocumented in our own data [2].

In the color library it falls among the greens at lightness 81, chroma 75, hue 150 degrees, close to [[malachite]] and [[teal]], and near a related xkcd entry the library calls Tealish Green, about two and a half units away [2]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would place the same hue in its "brilliant yellowish green" block, six units off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color within four units of Weird Green covering at least one per cent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. Bright, cool, minty greens like this are rare in historical pigments, which tend toward duller earths and verdigris rather than this clean a mint [3]. In printed English the exact phrase *weird green* is uncommon; it appears sporadically from the 1890s with no clear peak [4].
